chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the 'Hamil' (a captive parent with a child). He said, 'And what is the Hamil?' I said, 'A woman is taken captive from her land, and with her is her young child, so she says, 'He is my son.' And a man is taken captive, and his brother meets him, so he says, 'He is my brother,' and they recognize each other, and there is no proof for them regarding that except their word.' He said, 'So what do they say on your side?' I said, 'They do not inherit him because there was no proof regarding that; it was merely childbirth in captivity.' He said, 'Glory be to God! When she brings her son or daughter with her, she remains affirming him, and when his brother recognizes him, and that is in the soundness of their intellects, they remain affirming that, and one inherits the other.'

key_terms.اَلْحَمِيلُ: A captive parent traveling with or separated from their young child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance between a captive mother and child who reunite based only on their word?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the prevailing view in the Shia community that separation during captivity severs inheritance ties, arguing instead that continuous maternal acknowledgment or mutual sibling recognition in a state of sound intellect constitutes sufficient proof. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential preference for *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and practical testimony over rigid formalistic requirements, ensuring family bonds remain legally intact despite political upheaval or war.
